diagnostic_evidence.quote: We derive an inapproximability threshold of $(2\sqrt{2}/3)^{1/k}$.

issues.failure_explanation: In the reduction k=M grows with the instance size, because X3C with fixed M is solvable in polynomial time. The gap factor (2sqrt2/3)^{1/k} therefore tends to 1, so 1-(2sqrt2/3)^{1/k} is about 0.059/k. A PTAS with any fixed epsilon has ratio 1-epsilon, which falls below this threshold for large k, so it cannot distinguish true from false instances. Choosing epsilon of order 1/k gives a non-polynomial running time for a general PTAS. The argument excludes only an FPTAS. The gap is also tight: in a false instance a single overlapping pair can make vol equal to 2sqrt2/3.

failure_location.quote: Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for S-optimality maximization.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either produce a reduction with a k-independent constant gap for S-optimality, or weaken the claim to 'no FPTAS unless P=NP'.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that S-optimality admits no PTAS (Table, contributions, abstract) is unsupported. NP hardness (t_voldec) is unaffected.
issues.title: Vanishing gap (2sqrt2/3)^{1/k} does not exclude a PTAS for S-optimality
issues.why_classification: The advertised no-PTAS guarantee is lost. Only the weaker no-FPTAS statement survives without a new reduction.

issues.failure_explanation: The decision problems in s_psnorm1 range over all k-column submatrices, but Lemma l_pinv, and Lemma l_fi used in t_pi, require rank(C)=k. Distinct 3-sets can be linearly dependent. Take K1={1,2,3}, K2={4,5,6}, K3={1,2,4}, K4={3,5,6}, with K1+K2=K3+K4. The Gram matrix of the four columns has eigenvalues 2, 4/3, 2/3, 0. Hence ||C^+||_F^2 = 1/2+3/4+3/2 = 2.75 < k = 4, although these sets are not disjoint. In a false X3C instance containing such sets, the Frobenius (and Schatten-p) pseudo-inverse decision problem answers 'yes', so the reduction is incorrect. The same example also breaks the gap bound of t_pi.

issues.failure_explanation: The false-instance bound ||C^+||_F^2 >= k+1/4 exceeds the optimum k only by the factor sqrt(1+1/(4k)), which tends to 1 as k=M grows. A (1+epsilon)-approximation with fixed epsilon cannot separate the cases for large k, so only an FPTAS is excluded. The bound is tight for this reduction: k-2 disjoint sets plus one pair sharing one element give exactly k+1/4. t_pi3 (via the vector p-norm relation) and t_fcond (multiplying by ||C||_F = sqrt(k)) inherit the same vanishing factor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hence, all singular values of $\mc$ are equal to~1, and $\mc$ has orthonormal columns.

issues.failure_explanation: rvol depends only on the ratios sigma_j/sigma_1, so rvol(C)=1 forces all singular values to be equal, not equal to 1. Counterexample: C = 2I_k has rvol = 1 but its columns are not orthonormal. The proof's step to 'equal to 1' is unjustified. It does hold under unit-norm columns, where sum sigma_j^2 = k, which is what thm:rvolnp actually uses.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\rvol(\mc) = 1$  if and only if the columns of $\mc$ are orthonormal.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis ||C e_j||_2 = 1 (or state the conclusion as 'C is a scalar multiple of a matrix with orthonormal columns'), and use (e_srk) to get sigma_j = 1.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the lemma is false. Its application in thm:rvolnp and t_volptas survives because those matrices have unit-norm columns.
issues.title: rvol(C)=1 does not imply orthonormal columns without a unit-norm hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A local added hypothesis fixes the lemma, and all uses remain valid.

issues.failure_explanation: From sigma_1(C) >= 1 one gets (k/sigma_1^p)^{1/p} <= k^{1/p}, not >= k^{1/p}. So the chain does not prove ||C^+||_(p) >= k^{1/p}. The claim itself is true, for example by Jensen applied to t^{-p/2} with sum sigma_j^2 = k, or by the nonnegativity of g in (e_84).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the step with the convexity argument: sum_j g(sigma_j) >= 0 from (e_84) directly gives ||C^+||_(p)^p >= k.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound used to set the optimal value in the Schatten-p pseudo-inverse decision problem is unproven as written.
issues.title: Inequality chain for Schatten-p norm of pseudo-inverse runs the wrong way
issues.why_classification: A short routine replacement, already essentially present in the proof, restores the statement unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For q = p/2 > 1, ||diag(X,Y)||_(q) = (||X||_(q)^q + ||Y||_(q)^q)^{1/q}, which is at most ||X||_(q) + ||Y||_(q); the claimed equality is false. The lemma itself fails: for C = I_2, C_1 = e_1, C_2 = e_2, the left side is 2^{2/p} < 2, which is the right side, for p > 2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the statement by the valid p-th power version ||C^+||_(p)^p >= ||C_1^+||_(p)^p + ||C_2^+||_(p)^p, which follows from the same pinching argument.
